QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_32

question.text: The SE Antyodaya Seva Sangh partners with the state's Mission Shakti. Under SAS-400, the 'deadweight' that the SIA should net out is:

answer.text: Proportion of the reported outcome that would have occurred anyway due to Mission Shakti or broader social trends, absent the SE's intervention
Number of SIAs on the panel

explanation.text: The Logic: Deadweight = outcomes that would have happened anyway without the SE's intervention (due to government schemes, social trends, etc.). SAS-400 SROI / net impact requires deadweight subtraction. Options B, C, D are irrelevant cost items. The Trap: Option B confuses deadweight with programme cost. Options C and D are not impact-assessment concepts. Cross-Exam Context: Deadweight logic also applicable in X-A / X-B (Investment Adviser — CSR attribution) and UK-Cabinet-Office SROI guidelines. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Estimate deadweight by finding the nearest 'comparator' (control) village or by citing a published control-group study. Disclose the deadweight % upfront in the SROI annexure.
